record_type_quote: The purpose of the present study is to replicate these findings, focusing on police in one city: Baltimore, Maryland.

targets.authors: Kachurik, S., Ruiz, J. & Staub, M.
targets.title: Police officers killed on duty: a different view.
targets.evidence_quote: The goal of the current research was to confirm the findings of Kachurik et al. (2013), namely that officers with social investment – officers with children – were less likely to be fatally killed while on duty.
targets.outcome_quote: Kachurik and colleagues also found that law enforcement officers with fewer than ten years of experience were killed at a lower rate than those with more than ten years. In the present research, these findings were partially supported. First, social investment was an important predictor of felonious deaths in the line of duty; however, here, only marriage, not children, emerged as the important predictor. Second, contrary to Kachurik et al. (2013), the current study found a negative relationship between officer experience and officer murder; that is, less tenured officers were more likely to be killed in the line of duty than their more experienced counterparts.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly state partial support and identify both an agreeing social investment relationship and differences in children, marriage and experience.

reasoning: A different historical Baltimore sample re-tests Kachurik et al. The historical data source is not itself a target. Other studies are background; incidental descriptive comparisons do not establish additional intended replication targets.
